blocks.content: Suppose our code has θ(n) time complexity. This means that for a sufficiently large input,

items: our code will complete the execution with θ(n) complexity;
it will never take θ(n2)θ(n^2)θ(n2) complexity (because the growth of n2n^2n2 is faster than that of n);
it will never take θ(n3)θ(n^3)θ(n3) complexity (because the growth of n3 is faster than that of n).

blocks.content: Essentially, the Theta notation tells us that if a program has a certain time complexity, let's say θ(log n), we can be certain that the time complexity of the program grows neither faster nor slower than θ(log n).
